front.title: Research on Computing Power Network Technology for Stateless Computing Services

abstract.t: Stateless computing services represent a principal design paradigm in distributed computing, characterized by statelessness, dynamism, service orientation, and atomicity. These services have been widely adopted in cloud computing and microservice architectures. With the rise of AI technologies and the emergence of Model-as-a-Service (MaaS), they are being introduced into intelligent computing, reshaping industrial divisions of labor and gradually evolving into a typical computing power provisioning paradigm following IaaS/PaaS. However, current computing power networks were found to primarily focus on resource-layer scheduling optimization, leading to critical challenges when addressing computing-network collaboration and routing/scheduling requirements for stateless services. These included the disconnection between computing resource scheduling and user application-layer functional demands, as well as protocol stack mismatches between network-layer connectivity solutions and service-oriented API interconnection requirements. The need for elastic network pipelines in computing service interconnection was analyzed, followed by the proposal of a novel computing power network architecture natively supporting stateless service routing and scheduling. Key components including the identifier scheme, system architecture, and operational mechanisms were detailed through simulation validation. URL-PATH is employed as computing power identifiers, enabling service-oriented API-level resource orchestration and differentiated QoS guarantees through service semantic routing. This approach provides new insights for evolving computing power networks from "resource provisioning" to "service interconnection."
